The rank list left no room for doubt. Harsha scrolled to the bottom of the admit list at six in the morning and did not find his number. By breakfast the sentence in his head had hardened: I am stupid, and Papa's money is wasted. He thought of the coaching fees, the extra tiffin his mother packed, and the way the whole family had planned its year around this one exam. A single test had become a verdict on all of him.

He told Lokesh, who texted twice, that the paper had been set unfairly and the invigilator had rushed them. Then he stopped replying to Lokesh and told nobody else. On Sunday his father asked, "Anything on the result?" and Harsha said, "Not up yet."

That evening at his aunt's house the truth reached the room anyway, through a neighbour's son. Over tea an uncle counted off cousins' ranks and glanced at Harsha. "Some children just don't apply themselves." His cousin Gopika, visiting from Hyderabad, watched Harsha's face go blank. She followed him to the balcony that same hour. "One result isn't you," she said. "Do you want to sit with me and work out what comes next?" He nodded without looking up, and then, to his own surprise, wept.

qa.q: What did Harsha tell his father on Sunday about the result?
qa.a: He said it was not up yet.

qa.q: How did Harsha's shame and hiding lead to the moment on the balcony?
qa.a: Harsha turned one failed test into a verdict that he was stupid and his father's money was wasted, then blamed the paper and hid the result. When the truth reached his aunt's house and an uncle counted off cousins' ranks, Gopika saw his face go blank and offered a quiet word that one result is not the person.

qa.q: What was Harsha feeling when the uncle counted off the cousins' ranks?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and numb, and his face went blank.

qa.q: What could the family do to support Harsha now?
qa.a: They could stop comparing him with cousins, say that one result is not the person, and sit down with him to plan next steps.

grounding: Shows a teen's failure arc: shame turning one test into a verdict on the self, blaming and hiding, and a cousin offering a quiet word and a plan when the family compares.
